scores.why: Keeps the glow and tube, but it is a wash of green on black with little variation, the very thing the owner asked to change.
Grounded slate with a real tube and a typed question, and the change shows across Home, Chat and Ideas. The lists are plain text rows with little line art, and the left column of Home ends in a void.
Signal Box's line language carried through Home, To do, Chat and Ideas, over slate with amber, cyan and a little violet. The tube keeps its glow and scanlines, and the page is calm.

A bold poster-type redesign that is unmistakably different, but the giant lit MIND is the brightest, most contrasty thing on any card, and the hatched orange, blue and green swatches drift from the CRT feel.
A console grid with lit rails, a NOW node and a To do timetable, which is the line art the owner loves, with real tube glow. The corner ticks and hatched blank plates add clutter.

Fixes the void in Desk Terminal's left column by docking Coming up and Contents under the tube, and adds a lit rail on To do. It is solid and grounded, but still the plainest list treatment of the field.

The rail from Vera's screen to the question box draws the eye through the page, and the 'was due N days ago' stamps and wide Add key give the content a clearer voice. Grounded colour, glowing key word with coarse scanlines, and the Signal Box lines carried through.
The chat hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark is lovely and the cool bone and steel suit the green. The poster MIND is still the loudest item on the page, and its look is far from the CRT original.

The best-calmed console: line art, lit track, NOW node and 44px targets, with the clutter of corner ticks and hatching removed. It keeps the tube glow where the phosphor is and is modern, grounded and still a CRT. The change is quiet at half size.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the calmed lattice, lit track and 44px system. Bring back one small lit signature on each cell (a top-edge highlight or a glowing corner dot) so the Grid keeps its console identity, and add the Home rail from Vera's screen to the box (from r19-mut-2).

Keep the rail from Vera's screen to the question box, the amber 'was due' stamps and the coarse scanlines in the key word. Make the rail thicker or add a node mid-way so it reads at half size, and give the greeting back the width it took from Next up so the tube does not wrap.
Keep the dock row and the lit rail on To do. Equalise the heights of Coming up and Contents. Borrow the Signal Box tracks and the amber stamps so the list rows stop reading as plain text.

Lift the rail chat thread and the cool bone and steel palette into a design with a calmer head. Tone the giant MIND down: lower the brightness, narrow the fill, and keep the halo and scanlines instead of a bright slab.
The poster type is a bold idea, but the lit word needs to sit lower in brightness. Replace the hatched orange, blue and green swatches with cyan or slate line icons.

judges.notes: The Signal Box family (Track Diagram, Grid Console) is where the owner's praise sits: thin lines that delimit areas and lead the eye, over grounded slate, with the tube glowing where the phosphor is. Of the two new entries in that family, Grid Console Calmer and Rail Keys are real, if modest, improvements on their parents. Desk Terminal is grounded and the best on the monitor (waveform, typed question, grid floor), but its lists are the plainest. Lit Index is the biggest visible change across every page, but it is also the brightest and most contrasty, and it is furthest from the CRT soul. It is worth developing only with calmer lit type. The yardstick (today) is clearly the least varied card.

parts.what: Vera's lit screen with a steel rail turning to the question box and ending at a lit lamp
To do on a vertical lit track with a 'now' node, amber 'was due' ladder at left and a DUE timetable margin
Thread hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark, times in the margin, a lit ring where the box begins
Green-black slate plates with amber for late, soft cyan and violet for kinds, and the bright green held back for the lit things
Condensed poster headings with a mono label scale and numbered running heads (runner-up: serif section heads with a lit numeral)
Key word with coarse scanlines and layered halo, the tube's bloom, and a grid floor in the monitor

scores.why: The yardstick: the key-word halo, one monitor and the glowing dots are all there, but the rest of the page is plain dark cards with little tube light, so only the corner and a few marks feel like a green screen.

The phosphor reaches across the pages: Vera's question is typed on a real tube with a LISTENING line, Status has a dial in a bezel, Ideas has a radar, and the Home chart has a perspective floor. Light stays on the glass and the surrounding page is grounded.

Same strongest tube set as r18-mut-1, plus Coming up docked under the glass and a lit rail down the To do rows, which carries the afterglow into the list. It is the most phosphor across content, with calm elsewhere.
One good scanlined key word and a bezelled radar monitor, but the cream serif heads and slate plates make the rest of the page quiet, so the tube is a lone island.

The rail from Vera's lit screen to a lamp at the question, and the coarser scanlines in the key word, add true light in the content. The cream serif and slate still make the page calm to the point of a little lifeless.

A giant scanlined MIND with a halo is the most striking lit word, and the beige-bezel monitor is period-true. But the poster type is more editorial than green screen, and Ideas and Status are mostly cream and hatched with little tube light.

Brightens and scanlines the poster key word to full phosphor and cools the bezel and neutrals, so the lit effect is stronger against slate. Rail and boxed ticks add small lit details. Still a lone big word, with a mismatched dim question mark.
A lit lattice, a NOW node, glowing track lines and a monitor with a grid floor give a console feel. The bright MIND is cropped and many outlined cells flatten the glow.

Calms the lattice and quiets the lead words so the key word and rail carry the light, which is tasteful. But it removes lit corner ticks, so it gives up some of the console glow, and the poster looks like the parent.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the tube set (typed question, dial, radar, chart) and the lit To do rail. Equalise the dock row so Coming up and the Contents plate end together, and bring Finish setting up back near the top on a fresh install.
Kept as the baseline. Its tubes are the strongest, but the dock gap and the blank column under Coming up are what r19-mut-1 fixes.
Keep the brighter, scanlined poster key word and the cool bezel. Brighten or scanline the question mark so it matches MIND, and carry a tube (dial or radar) onto Status so the light is not one word.

Keep the head-to-box rail with its lamp and the coarse-scanline key word. Anchor the lamp to the question line so a wrapped line cannot leave it off, and give the Status and Ideas heads a lit element so the glow is not confined to Home.
Keep the calmer lattice and the 44px targets. Put back one lit feature per cell, such as a glowing top edge on hover or active, so the console has light and not only line.

judges.notes: The Desk Terminal line wins on soul because the green screens carry the page content: the typed question with its LISTENING status, the dial, the radar and the chart each sit in a real bezel, and the light stays on the glass while the page around them is grounded. That meets the owner's request for the original's tube effect without going back to a green wash. The Lit Index (r19-mut-3) has the single strongest lit word, a scanlined, haloed MIND, but its light is confined to that word and the Ideas and Status heads are cream and hatched. The Track Diagram (r19-mut-2) has a good idea in the rail and lamp, but its cream serif and slate are very calm. The Grid Console (r19-mut-4) shows good discipline in calming the lattice. Its lit key word is half-cropped, and calming it removed some console glow. The differences between r19-mut-1 and r18-mut-1 are small and mostly lower on the page, which my cards show only partly. The r19 mutations are mostly modest changes to their parents, so the real contest is between the families, and Desk Terminal leads.

parts.what: Key word as a bright #6dff9c gradient with scanlines and a strong halo, so the poster word is the lit centrepiece
Vera's question typed in glyph type with a block cursor on a tube, with a LISTENING status line, plus a docked Contents plate and status under the tube
Poster question with a bright scanlined key word and a bone head; or the baseline-aligned title, count and deck line
Steel rail from Vera's lit screen to a lit lamp at the question box; the glowing live dot and NOW node on the track
Spend dial in a bezelled tube (needle, tick scale, LIMIT flag), plus the radar and the chart with a lit floor grid

scores.why: Lovely halo and tube, but a sea of near-identical green-glowing cards with one voice and no typographic personality; this is the 'Matrix' the family named.
Terminal with a typed question, a status line and a contents plate is tidy and grounded, but it reads as a well-made dashboard; the type is one voice and the identity is polite.
Docking Coming up under the card fixes the void and the lit rail on To do is a nice touch, but it is the same dashboard with the same sans and little new mood.
A serif display face for Vera and the lilac Ideas numeral, with a steel rail and lit nodes down the chat, give an editorial, instrument-panel feel unlike any stock dark theme.
Adds the rail running from Vera's screen to the question box and the amber 'was due 6 days ago', so the head-to-box path reads as one idea; refined and warmer, though the rail is faint at size.

The poster question in tall condensed type with a scanlined, glowing MIND, the numbered 00-05 index, the colour-coded section bars and hatched kind swatches make a bold, memorable, genuinely new identity, with phosphor light only where it counts.

Keeps the Lit Index poster identity and brightens MIND; the chat hung on a rail from Vera's mark, with margin times and cool bone and steel in place of cream and brass, carries the personality into the conversation. The dim ? beside a brighter MIND is the one flaw.
Condensed headers, numbered cells, a lit track with a NOW node and the grid-floor lamp footer make a coherent control-room language, but the lattice and hatching are busy.
Calming the lattice and aligning head baselines is sensible and tidier, but it loses some console identity and the difference is quiet at half size.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster MIND, the rail chat with margin times and the cool bone and steel. Light the question mark to match MIND, or drop it a step, so the two do not look unmatched, and carry the poster headings and rail down to Plans, To do and Settings.
Keep the index nav and the colour-coded section bars as the system. Fix the dim question mark, and give the chat the rail thread so the conversation is as designed as Home.
The rail from Vera's screen to the box is the best new idea here. Thicken it and let it glow a little so it shows at half size, and anchor the lamp to the box by layout, not a hand-tuned offset.
Keep the lit track, the NOW node and the condensed heads. Thin the lattice and hatched plates (as Calmer began to) but keep one lit corner mark per cell so it still reads as a console.
Keep the 44px target system and the baseline heads. Restore a little lit-corner identity, in the primary cell only, so calm does not become plain.

judges.notes: The two Lit Index entries stand out: a poster-scale scanlined MIND, a numbered index and colour-coded section bars have a point of view that a family would remember and that nothing generic offers. The Rail and Grid families are coherent and grounded, but they are more dashboard than character. The Desk Terminal pair is competent and the most predictable. All the new designs differ from today across the pages, not just in a corner. The best new ideas are the rail threads (the chat on a rail from her mark, and the rail from the tube to the box). Their weak point is that they are faint at size.

parts.what: Tall condensed poster headings with a mono index and small caps labels; serif display as the alternative voice
Cool bone ink and steel labels on slate plates, with the green kept for light and the hatched kind swatches as the accents
Poster question with a bright scanlined MIND, a listening line and a ruled input
Numbered sections under colour-tipped hairline bars, with a big condensed title and a small count beneath
Typed question on a CRT screen with a LISTENING status line, plus a rail from the tube to the box
Numbered 00-05 index tabs with lettered utilities on the right; a lamp and grid-floor footer as the alternative

scores.why: Coherent and legible, but the whole Home is one green wash with a small Send icon, a cramped starter row and a squinted view where nothing leads; the yardstick.
Tube with typed question, Listening lamp, bars and a grounded slate card give a clear title, then question, then action path; the Send is still a small icon beside the mic.
Real scanlined key word and a good radar monitor, but the composer is cramped and the Next up title wraps to three lines on the phone.
The poster MIND leads the squint test and the Send is a full-width key, so the eye goes title, action, content; the cream/brass tint and glow are a little heavy and the poster eats the first screen.
Grid cells give the Home structure and the poster question reads well with a plain Send icon, but the lattice, corner ticks and violet accents add visual noise and 20 targets are under 44px.
Keeps the best glass and adds a full-width Send with its word and a taller composer, a real phone gain; docking Coming up beside the tube improves the Home but pushes Finish setting up down.
The rail and lamp from Vera's screen to the box is a lovely idea, but the cost is a cramped phone composer: the textarea clips its placeholder and the select wraps to two lines.

Strongest first-screen hierarchy: a bright MIND, a full-width Send and a lit-tick checkbox; cool bone and steel replace the brass and the light is brought back on the key word; 44px nav and boxed controls hold up on a phone at night.
Calmer lattice and every target at 44px (0 under) make it the most usable grid, but the greyed lead words and quiet outlines make it close to its parent at a glance.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster question, full Send key, lit-tick boxed controls and the cool palette. Fix the dim '?' next to the bright MIND, and keep the poster to about a third of the phone's first screen so the starters show above the fold.
Keep the big Send with its word and the Vera card with its tube and Listening line. Equalise the dock row's heights, and keep Finish setting up prominent for a fresh install.

Keep the steel rail with its lamp from Vera's screen to the box. On the phone keep the select on one line and the textarea two lines tall, which means giving the rail less indent (about 34px is too much).

Keep the 44px --hit token and the baseline heads. Bring back some lit identity in the cells (one lit edge or an icon tint) so the calm does not read as the old page, and lift the greyed lead words of the question.
The poster is the strongest squint-test lead. Pull the cream back to a cool neutral as in r19-mut-3 and soften the halo on the large letters.

judges.notes: On the use cards, the poster-question designs (Lit Index family) and Desk Terminal with a full Send key lead the eye title, then action, then content most clearly, and the Lit Index family brings back the most tube light on the key word without glare elsewhere. The Grid Console family is the most consistent as a system and r19-mut-4 is the cleanest on targets, but it is the closest to today at half size. The Track Diagram rail is a charming idea that costs phone composer room, which is a real task cost for sending Vera a message. r19-mut-1's big Send and docked Coming up are the best task-oriented changes; r19-mut-3's boxed controls and cool material are the best system-level changes. All designs far exceed today on grounded colour and hierarchy.

parts.what: Boxed controls: lit-tick checkbox frame, select with a caret cell, full-width Send key, 44px nav
Uppercase tab bar of divided 44px cells with a clear lit active cell
Listening lamp and level bars on the tube's status line; a lit lamp where the rail meets the box
Vera card: tube with typed question, tall composer, FROM select, mic and a big Send key, starters below
Poster question with a bright gradient MIND and a running head 'VERA  SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER'

scores.why: Black ground with one green on everything, flat grey cards and bare heads. It is monochrome and the owner calls it too contrasty, though the halo is real.

The tube-and-dial rail on every page is across-the-page content, and the slate case and amber 'was due' are grounded. It has only two or three lit moments and a lot of the same boxed panel, and the sidebar plus tube crowd a narrow page.

Serif display titles with a count, a lit chain down Who answers, a dated timeline with a NOW node and a clock on Plans change all four pages, and the tube keeps the light. The serif could read as editorial or costume in places, but the cream and steel are grounded and the type is clearly the best here.

Heavy condensed titles, indexed numbers and coloured rules change the page structure on every card, and the type is distinctive. It is shouty: Settings is a wall of huge condensed words, and the light is thin (a small tube and a few rules), so the phosphor feeling is mostly gone.

The strongest tube light and glow and a lit trunk through the page, with a clear ledger of cells and a NOW node. Hatched plates, grid lines and cool outlines are busy and edge toward the editor or Matrix-HUD look, and the cell grid feels repeated on every page.

On the lists cards it is a near duplicate of r18-mut-1; the only visible change is a thin green rail on To do rows. The Home dock row is not visible here, so the difference is mostly out of sight and the dock row has an equal-height gap by its own admission.

The Track Diagram parent plus a wide bright Add key, amber 'was due N days ago' and a Plans keycap tray. The full-width glowing green Add bar on To do is glare and out of keeping with the calmer pages, though the plain-spoken overdue stamps are a real gain.

Lit Index with cool bone and steel replacing cream and brass. The lists cards barely differ from the parent apart from a slightly cooler Plans cell, and a boxed select. It is a refinement, not a new idea, and the cool tint is hard to see.

Grid Console with the corner ticks and hatching removed, so the page is calmer and cleaner and the heads sit on one baseline. It answers the clutter I flagged in head-5, but it is the same page as head-5 at half size, and the grid still looks like an editor or HUD.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the serif titles with counts, the lit chain, the timeline and the clock. Make the display serif less cream-heavy (a bit greyer) so it does not read as costume, and add a little more light to the green hairlines.
Keep the amber 'was due N days ago' stamp. Replace the full-width glowing Add bar with a compact right-aligned primary key so the bright green stays a signature, not glare.
Keep the calmer lattice and baseline-aligned heads. Bring back one or two quiet lit marks (the NOW node and trunk) and enlarge the differences from head-5, which are invisible at half size.
Keep the indexed numbers and the coloured rule under each title. Take the title size down one step on Settings, where the condensed type becomes a wall, and let the tube carry more of the light.
Keep the tube, dial and keycap tray. Let the side rail collapse to the tube alone on narrower pages so the content gets its width.

judges.notes: The field is split into four families, and the r19 mutants are mostly small edits on their parents, so several cards are near duplicates. That is exactly what the owner objected to ("those look nearly identical"). The Track Diagram and Grid Console lines do most for the owner's complaint: they change the structure of every page (headers with counts, a timeline with a NOW node, section trunks) and keep real tube light. Lit Index is typographically bold, but it trades light for volume and its r19 cool-rail variant is invisible on these cards. Desk Terminal is solid and grounded, and its r19 docked track adds only a thin rail on the lists pages. Today's page scores low because the single green carries everything.

parts.what: serif display title with a lit-ring icon and a small count and subhead on the same baseline
timeline rows with dated amber pips, the NOW node and a plain 'was due N days ago' stamp
the cost tube with its dial, plus the Plans clock showing the week's past, today and ahead
a lit trunk rail with section heads branching off it, and cells drawn by fill and edge
a vertical lit chain down Who answers, with steel hollow rings for off and amber for needs a look
keycap-tray filters with a lit pip on the held key, and a compact bright Add key
